itinerary.cal: Boston Basin camping requires winning NPS's early-access permit lottery (~15% odds); Cascade River Road's opening date varies with winter road damage. This is one of the Fifty Classic Climbs of North America, so weekend permits are especially competitive.

days.note: Hike the climbers' path from the trailhead into Boston Basin and camp near 6,400 ft below the peak.
days.title: Approach to Boston Basin camp

days.note: Pre-dawn start up the approach couloir to the West Ridge notch, then ~6 pitches of low 5th-class ridge climbing to the true summit. Reverse the ridge to the notch and descend the couloir back to camp, hiking out the same evening or the next morning.

days.objective: Climb the West Ridge and return to camp

itinerary.totalNote: A 2-day trip for most parties (hike in/camp, then an 8-10 hr technical summit day); very strong parties occasionally push it car-to-car in a single ~17.5-hr day.

weather.typical: Cool mornings, warming through the day; a prime but weather-sensitive summer window.
weather.probability: Afternoon thunderstorms are a recurring hazard, especially in July-August.

seasonal_hazards.exposure: Sustained, committing exposure along the knife-edge summit ridge crest; a fall would be serious to fatal, and a multi-rappel descent is required.

avalanche.zone: West Slopes North (NWAC catchment); NWAC issues no daily forecast between roughly mid-April and mid-November, so no live rating covers this route's July-Sept season

seasonal_hazards.crevasses: N/A - no glacier travel; the approach couloir/gully is a snow-and-scree feature, not a glacier.

fitnessSpec.hiking: Strenuous - roughly 7 miles and 3,100+ ft gain to Boston Basin camp with an overnight pack, plus a pre-dawn approach to the notch.
fitnessSpec.packWeight: Overnight alpine pack, typically 25-35 lb including rack, rope, and camp gear.

partner_requirements.approachTime: ~5-6 hrs to Boston Basin camp, then ~2-3 hrs pre-dawn to the west ridge notch.
requiredSkills: snow travel with ice axe and crampons in the access couloir
route-finding on an exposed ridge crest
efficient party movement to avoid holding up others on a crowded route
partner_requirements.experienceLevel: Intermediate alpine climber; solid multi-pitch trad leader comfortable on exposed 5.6 with prior snow travel experience.

climbing_route.label: Lower face rock below the ice patch
climbing_route.notes: From the Boston Glacier, start up the rock immediately below and left of the conspicuous ice patch on the lower face. This first section runs about 300 ft and was recorded on the first ascent as grade III climbing protected with a few pitons. Getting off the glacier and onto the rock involves the usual moat or bergschrund at the margin, which grows through the season. Note that this face is climbed rarely enough that no maintained fixed gear should be assumed and modern first-hand descriptions are scarce, so treat this outline as an outline.

climbing_route.label: The ice patch
climbing_route.notes: The route's technical centrepiece: roughly 300 ft of ice at about 50 degrees. It is a north-facing feature that has thinned across the range over recent decades, so the depth of ice available for screws should be verified on the day rather than assumed. Everything on the face above funnels through this section, making it the exposed spot for rock and ice released from higher up.

climbing_route.label: Upper face to the summit
climbing_route.notes: About 600 ft remain above the ice patch. The angle is steep, but the rock is laid in upward-dipping slabs which makes the climbing easier than it looks from below. Above this the face merges into the summit. Descent is not by reversing the face — the normal descent is a high traverse below the east ridge that skirts the ridge gendarmes rather than following the crest, and it is a long committing exit in its own right; the peak has a reputation for having no easy way down by any route.

before.descent: Descend via the standard descent route, retracing the ascent when possible. Be aware of loose rock and snow bridge hazards. Maintain group cohesion on exposed sections.
obj_haz: documented fatal fall on the traverse (1975)
confusing route-finding across multiple rock ribs

before.itinerary: Used as the descent leg after climbing the West Ridge, East Ridge Direct, or Northwest Face; not typically a stand-alone objective.

before.descent: Descend the West Ridge to its notch and couloir, or reverse the East Ridge with rappels.
before.watch_out:
Glacier approach with crevasse field—continuous rope essential; probe every step; bergschrund crossing required at ridge base
Moat crossing at ridge base—seasonal variation; late season moats can be 5-10+ feet with difficult crossing; assess before committing
Loose rock sections on east ridge—unstable granite typical of area; test holds; rockfall potential from upper sections and other climbers
Route-finding on initial ridge sections—terrain confusing with multiple false summits; verify correct line; study photos and topo
Weather exposure on high ridge—exposed position with altitude gain to 8400 ft; afternoon storms common; lightning hazard
Descent complexity—rappel setup required on some sections; route-finding important in descent; tired climbers increase risk
Sustained high-altitude objective—7000+ ft elevation gain to base; hydration and energy management critical; altitude sickness possible
Potential avalanche exposure on approach slopes—assess stability in spring; afternoon warming increases risk; early start essential

before.beta: Grade III, 5.7 climbing. From Boston Basin high camp, traverse glacier to Sharkfin Col via 10 feet of 5.7 rock and 200 feet of Class 3 gully. Northeast ridge route at ~7,700 ft to summit. Moderate to good granite, high exposure with wonderful ridge position. Glaciers: Quien Sabe Glacier, Boston Glacier.
before.watch_out:
Winter route requiring ice climbing or snow climbing skills
Short ice pitch potential in winter conditions
Alpine terrain exposure in winter conditions
Remote location increases rescue difficulty
before.approach: North-northeast via glacier traversals. From Boston Basin parking, hike to Boston Basin high camp (~5700 ft). Traverse moraine and west edge of Quien Sabe Glacier to 7,500 ft. Climb to Sharkfin Col (7,720 ft).
